Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. Branch: feature/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches. Build mode. This is SFCC-91 Step 2 of 4, REWORK round 2 (following your own round-1 REWORK verdict). Do not commit, do not stage — you may read/investigate freely.

## Your own round-1 verdict (for reference — you wrote this)

REWORK, for exactly one confirmed defect: `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts:31` set `backgroundColor: 'var(--zimm-color-background-02)'`, a CSS custom property that does not exist anywhere in the registry (the real one is `--zimm-color-bg-02`), making the swatch background always render transparent instead of ivory in every state. You gave a narrow, exact instruction: change exactly three single-line occurrences of `-background-02` to `-bg-02` — `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts:31`, `index.test.tsx:112` (the assertion), `index.test.tsx:31` (a comment quoting the same wrong literal) — and touch nothing else, since everything else (the two-part structure, bottom-border/selected logic, focus-ring mirroring, deliberate omission of a name-derived backgroundColor) was already independently confirmed correct in round 1 by both the Tester and by you.

## What happened since

An Implementer round made exactly those three substitutions. I (the orchestrating session, not a sub-agent) then independently re-verified directly myself, right now, rather than trusting either the implementer's or a fresh tester's report:

```
grep -n "zimm-color-bg-02\|zimm-color-background" overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/zimmColourSwatch.css.ts overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/index.test.tsx
```
→ three hits, all now reading `zimm-color-bg-02`, zero remaining `zimm-color-background` anywhere.

```
grep -rn "zimm-color-background" overrides/
```
→ zero hits anywhere in the entire `overrides/` tree — the wrong name is completely gone, not just from the three cited spots.

I also ran, myself, directly:
- `npx tsc --noEmit` → 0 errors.
- `npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/index.test.tsx` → 8/8 passing, including the regression-guard test that was previously passing vacuously against the wrong literal.
- `npm run test` (full suite) → 27 files / 417 tests, all passing — identical count to the pre-rework baseline, confirming no test was added, removed, or newly broken.

I did not personally re-run a live Chromium/Playwright check this round (the round-1 Tester already did that, proving the mechanism: an unresolvable `var()` with no fallback computes to `transparent` for a non-inherited property — that CSS-spec behaviour doesn't change based on which token name is used, only whether the corrected name is now real, which I've confirmed by direct registry lookup: `overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts:54` registers `--zimm-color-bg-02` exactly).

Nothing else was touched: `git status --porcelain` shows only `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` (pre-existing 2-line registration from round 1, untouched by this rework) and the untracked `zimmColourSwatch/` directory. `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx` remains fully committed from Step 1 (`9f46912`), no working-tree diff.

## Your job

Given the fix is confirmed applied exactly as you specified, with the wrong token name now entirely absent from the codebase and all gates green (including the specific regression-guard test that was the whole point), re-score and issue a final verdict. You do not need to re-derive everything from scratch — the round-1 findings for everything NOT touched by this fix (the two-part structure, border/focus-ring logic, `href` branching, a11y surface, restraint/scope) still stand as you and the Tester already confirmed them; your job now is specifically to confirm the one thing that was wrong is actually fixed and nothing new broke. If you want to spot-check anything yourself before signing off rather than accepting my re-verification at face value, do so — but state plainly if you're relying on round-1 evidence versus something you checked yourself in this round.

State your final PASS/REWORK verdict, and if PASS, confirm explicitly whether this step is now ready to commit (i.e., whether a visual checkpoint is still owed given this was a pure bugfix to an already-existing recipe with no new callers wired up yet — same reasoning as your own Design-fidelity axis would apply to an unreachable/cosmetic-only change, or whether this specific fix, which changes an actual visible rendered value from transparent to ivory, is different enough from that reasoning that a real visual check is still warranted before commit).

1	import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
2	
3	/**
4	 * Recipe for a single PDP colour swatch — a clickable rectangle filled with that colour
5	 * variation's product photo. Two parts: `swatch` is the outer clickable box (geometry,
6	 * background, border, focus ring); `image` is the element carrying the dynamic
7	 * background-image fill — the URL itself cannot live here, see the component's own comment on
8	 * why that one `__css` spread stays dynamic.
9	 *
10	 * Values below are read directly off Figma for the three states this recipe distinguishes, not
11	 * estimated from surrounding metadata — Unselected (node 40000307:13826), Selected
12	 * (40000307:13831), Focus (40002689:3839), all under `size=Large/Rectangle`.
13	 */
14	export const ZimmColourSwatch = {
15	  parts: ['swatch', 'image'],
16	
17	  baseStyle: ({ selected }: { selected?: boolean }): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
18	    swatch: {
19	      display: 'inline-block',
20	      cursor: 'pointer',
21	      // Figma's Rectangle width (48px). Height (72px) has no direct token — the named scale has
22	      // nothing between 64px and 140px — so it's expressed as an aspect ratio on the width
23	      // instead. 2:3, not the incidentally different ratio Figma's raw code-gen attached to the
24	      // placeholder product photo pasted into that frame instance: the Selected-state node
25	      // carries its own dev annotation reading "Image aspect ratio - 2:3", which is the number
26	      // to trust here.
27	      width: 'var(--zimm-scale-1200)',
28	      aspectRatio: '2 / 3',
29	      // Identical across Unselected/Selected/Focus — ivory[200] / background['02'] in
30	      // theme/foundation/colour.ts.
31	      backgroundColor: 'var(--zimm-color-bg-02)',
32	      // Selected: a bottom-only border — the raw Figma export is unambiguous, a `border-b`
33	      // utility rather than a full box border. Colour is grey[900] / border.focus, the only
34	      // alias-tier value that resolves to it (border.default and border.secondary are both
35	      // light greys and never appear anywhere in this design).
36	      ...(selected
37	        ? {
38	            borderBottomWidth: 'var(--zimm-border-width-default)',
39	            borderBottomStyle: 'solid',
40	            borderBottomColor: 'var(--zimm-color-border-focus)',
41	          }
42	        : {}),
43	      // Focus: Figma draws this as the Selected baseline plus a ring at slightly asymmetric
44	      // per-side offsets, same colour. Not replicated literally — there is no other precedent
45	      // anywhere in this codebase for a non-uniform ring, and the asymmetry reads as that one
46	      // frame instance's export noise rather than a deliberate design decision. Mirrors
47	      // zimmNavItem.css.ts's own focus-ring block instead: a uniform `outline` + `outlineOffset`
48	      // pair, applied independently of `selected` above — a swatch can be focused without being
49	      // selected, and selected without being focused. `--zimm-focus-ring` already composites the
50	      // same border-width/colour pair used above; `--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default` matches
51	      // three of Figma's four side offsets.
52	      _focusVisible: {
53	        outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)',
54	        outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)',
55	      },
56	    },
57	    image: {
58	      display: 'block',
59	      width: '100%',
60	      height: '100%',
61	      backgroundSize: 'cover',
62	      backgroundPosition: 'center',
63	      backgroundRepeat: 'no-repeat',
64	    },
65	  }),
66	};
67

## Verdict: PASS (for this round's rework scope)

I independently re-derived every claim in the re-verification report rather than accepting it — reading the actual files, re-running the greps and gates myself, and walking the token-resolution chain by hand. Everything holds. One axis is explicitly **UNVERIFIED**, not passed — see below, and see the direct answer to your commit-readiness question at the end.

### Per-axis table (most severe/least-resolved first)

| Axis | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Design fidelity** | **UNVERIFIED** | The fix is proven correct through a complete non-visual chain (below), but no one — not the Implementer, not you, not me — has rendered the corrected component in an actual browser or Storybook this round. `grep -rn "ZimmColourSwatch"` outside its own folder returns only the theme registration — this component has **zero live-page callers**, so no later integration step will supply this check "for free" either. |
| Correctness | PASS — CONFIRMED (checked myself) | `npx tsc --noEmit` → 0 errors. Scoped `vitest run .../index.test.tsx` → 8/8. Full `npm run test` → 27 files / 417 tests, all green, identical count to baseline. `recipeGuards.test.ts` (the bare-token guard) → 6/6. |
| Pass criteria | PASS — CONFIRMED (checked myself) | All three round-1-specified single-line substitutions are exactly applied: `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts:31`, `index.test.tsx:31` (comment), `index.test.tsx:112` (assertion) — all read `zimm-color-bg-02`. Whole-tree `grep -rn "zimm-color-background" overrides/` → zero hits. Loose case-insensitive typo sweep (`zimm-colou?r-back?ground|zimm-color-bg`) → zero near-miss variants; the fix matches the exact `--zimm-color-bg-0N` convention already used identically in 5 other files (footer, zimmButton, zimmModal, header, zimmSubscribeSection). |
| Conformance | PASS — CONFIRMED (checked myself) | Uses the `var(--zimm-*)` form per `overrideStyling.md` hierarchy point 2, not a bare key. `index.tsx` sets **no** competing `bg`/`backgroundColor` prop that could override the recipe via Chakra's style-prop-after-`__css` precedence — read the file directly; the `name`-derived tint is deliberately, permanently omitted with a documented rationale. |
| Completeness | PASS — round 1 finding, reconfirmed present | `index.stories.tsx` and `index.test.tsx` both still present, folder listing confirms only the 2 files named in the round-1 instruction (`index.test.tsx`, `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts`) carry this round's timestamp — content of the story itself not re-litigated, per your scoping. |
| Restraint | PASS — CONFIRMED (checked myself) | `git diff -- overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` is exactly the pre-existing 2-line registration (1 import + 1 entry), nothing else. `git status --porcelain` shows nothing else touched. |

### What I tried to falsify

- Searched for **remaining exact occurrences** of the wrong token anywhere in `overrides/` — none.
- Ran a **loose, case-insensitive typo sweep** (`zimm-colou?r-back?ground|zimm-color-bg`) in case a near-miss variant (British spelling, case mismatch, off-by-one digit) slipped past an exact-string check — none found; confirmed the fix matches an established naming convention used in 5 unrelated files, not a one-off.
- Read `index.tsx` looking for a **competing style prop** that could override the recipe's corrected value at render time — none exists; the `name`-derived background tint is deliberately, permanently omitted with a three-point rationale in-file.
- Walked the **full token-resolution chain by hand**, since "the token exists in the registry" isn't the same claim as "it resolves to the intended colour": `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts:31` → `zimmTokens.ts:54` (`'--zimm-color-bg-02': colors.background['02']`) → `colour.ts:52` (`background['02'] = ivory[200]`) → `colour.ts:22` (`ivory[200] = '#f6f4f1'`). Confirmed it resolves to a real, sensible ivory hex, not an empty or placeholder value.
- **Re-ran tsc, the scoped test, and the full suite myself** rather than accepting the reported numbers.
- **Diffed** `theme/components/index.ts` myself and cross-checked file timestamps in the component folder to confirm scope discipline.

### What I could not verify

- **No live browser/Storybook render of the corrected component happened this round**, by anyone. jsdom, per the test file's own documented limitation (`index.test.tsx:28-36`), does not substitute CSS custom properties — the passing regression-guard test proves the *source declaration* is now correct, not the *resolved pixel*. This is the Design fidelity axis's UNVERIFIED case, named plainly rather than inferred as passing from green gates.
- I did **not** re-run round 1's live Chromium/Playwright check myself — I'm relying on your/the Tester's report that it demonstrated the transparent-background failure mode under the old token. The CSS mechanism it relied on (an invalid `var()` reference with no fallback, on a non-inherited property, computes to that property's initial value — `transparent` for `background-color`) is deterministic per the CSS Custom Properties spec, not something I'm taking on faith beyond that citation, but I'm flagging the provenance as round-1, not this-round.
- I did not re-review the parts of `index.tsx`/the recipe that round 1 already signed off on beyond the specific spot-check above (href branching, focus-ring offsets, border logic) — those stand on round-1 evidence per your scoping, not re-derived by me.

### Defects

None found this round.

### Commit-readiness — direct answer to your question

**Not yet.** This is not the unreachable/cosmetic-only case where skipping a live visual check is defensible. Three things distinguish it:

1. The fix changes an actual rendered value from invisible to visible (transparent → `#f6f4f1` ivory fill) — exactly the category of change this framework's own cautionary precedent (`width: 'xl'` blowing up spacing while passing tsc/eslint/vitest/CodeRabbit/Storybook a11y) says can't be cleared by green gates alone.
2. The component has **no live-page callers yet** — there is no future integration step guaranteed to incidentally supply this check. If it ships un-rendered and something in the chain is still visually off (even though the declaration chain is now correct), it may not surface for two more steps.
3. This repo deliberately has no visual-regression tooling in the automated suite (`testing.md`: "Storybook visual snapshots — Chromatic/Loki belongs in a separate budget, not Vitest") — so nothing automated will ever perform this check in place of a human.

Concrete, minimal way to close it before commit: open `index.stories.tsx`'s `Default`/`Selected`/`WithoutLink` stories in Storybook and confirm the swatch box now shows a visible ivory (`#f6f4f1`) fill in the unselected/selected/focus states, matching the three Figma nodes cited in the recipe's own header comment (`40000307:13826`, `40000307:13831`, `40002689:3839`). This is a ~2-minute look, not a new development cycle — I wouldn't model it as a third REWORK round on the Implementer, since there's no further code change implied; it's the one verification action still owed before this step is fully done.

### Biggest residual risk if this ships as-is

The declaration chain is airtight, but nobody has looked at a pixel. If `background['02']`/`ivory[200]` is the wrong *shade* of ivory against the real product photography (as opposed to simply "a valid registered token"), that would still pass every gate checked this round and only surface once a later step wires this into a live PDP.
